articles.headline: Why the Chiefs and Bills can give thanks to 2017 trade that landed Mahomes in KC
articles.description: Kansas City traded up for Patrick Mahomes, while Buffalo got a franchise left tackle and several Pro Bowlers.
articles.body:
"Don't get scared now."

On April 27, 2017, former Buffalo Bills general manager Doug Whaley arrived in his office for Day 1 of the draft and was quickly confronted with that four-word message. John Dorsey, then general manager of the Kansas City Chiefs, had first approached Whaley at the combine in February about making a trade for the Bills' No. 10 pick.

Two months later, with the draft set to begin, the Chiefs were focused.

Whaley believed the Bills were in "quarterback purgatory." The roster was good enough to contend for the playoffs, but without a franchise passer, that was its ceiling.

The Bills could use the No. 10 pick on a quarterback with franchise-altering potential. But Whaley had a few reservations. First, new Bills coach Sean McDermott didn't want to lose the locker room with a rookie quarterback whose presence could signal a rebuild with veteran Tyrod Taylor running the show.

And second, Whaley -- along with advisors Jim Monos and Ron Hughes -- identified 2018 as a year with enough quarterback talent to snag a top-five-caliber passer outside the top five, making it easier to navigate trades to find the right guy.

All that said, Whaley wouldn't have had a problem using a late first-round selection in 2017 on a quarterback if that pick came as part of a haul. And with the Chiefs coming off a 12-4 season led by Pro Bowl quarterback Alex Smith, Whaley felt confident Dorsey wasn't moving into the top 10 for a quarterback.

So Whaley heeded Dorsey's plea. He didn't get scared.

"We always felt like draft day there should be no surprises," Whaley told ESPN. "You should be ready for everything. So what we did was as soon as we were on the clock we just gave it seven minutes to see if anybody else wanted to call and beat the offer. No one called. So we hung up and I called [Dorsey] back and said, 'Let's get it done.'"

The Bills traded the No. 10 pick to Kansas City in exchange for picks Nos. 27 and 91 plus a 2018 first-round pick.

With that capital, and some additional draft-night maneuvering made possible with those picks, the Bills ended up with two-time All-Pro cornerback Tre'Davious White, five-time Pro Bowl left tackle Dion Dawkins, two-time Pro Bowl linebacker Tremaine Edmunds and wide receiver Zay Jones -- plus the flexibility to wait a year and ultimately pick MVP quarterback Josh Allen in 2018.

The draft haul was instrumental in turning a 17-year playoff drought into a new golden era for Buffalo. In the near-decade since, the Bills have been one of the NFL's winningest franchises -- second behind only the Chiefs -- and are second to Kansas City in playoff games played.

But the franchise-altering trade also came at a cost. With the 10th pick in 2017, the Chiefs selected Patrick Mahomes -- the two-time MVP, three-time Super Bowl champion and three-time Super Bowl MVP who has since stood in the way of Buffalo reaching an elusive Super Bowl, posting a 4-0 record against them in the playoffs.

articles.headline: How Jeffery Simmons changed the Bears' defensive identity
articles.description: Simmons' impact isn't just measured by his own numbers, but also by how he has elevated his teammates.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons had an idea, but he needed an unselfish act from defensive end Austin Booker to make it work.

The Bears were leading the New Orleans Saints 21-10 late in the fourth quarter Sunday, and coming out of the two-minute warning, the Saints were driving deep in Bears' territory. On first-and-10 from the 24-yard line, Simmons asked Booker to switch positions for one play.

Since he joined the Bears before their Week 8 game in Seattle, Simmons has been double-teamed 92 times, tied for the most in the NFL. He thought if he could line up at end, he could work 1-on-1 against rookie right tackle Mason Murphy.

He was right.

Booker made the switch, and Simmons got down in a four-point stance and ripped through Murphy's inside shoulder. He made his way into the New Orleans backfield in 0.72 seconds -- his second-fastest get-off rate this season -- before wrapping his orange-sleeved arms around quarterback Tyler Shough and hurtling him to the ground.

Simmons rose to his feet and pointed at the Bears' sideline, celebrating his third sack of the afternoon -- which tied a career high set in Week 9 of the 2021 season with the Tennessee Titans.

While fans in Soldier Field erupted around him, quarterback Caleb Williams stayed seated on the bench, offering little more than a knowing nod at his teammate of less than a month.

What used to feel like a game-changing splash play has become almost standard operating procedure for the Bears' defense, and Williams watched it unfold with the calm detachment of a quarterback who has already factored Simmons' dominance into the game plan.

"He's so good," said Williams, who then said he appreciated general manager Ryan Poles and coach Ben Johnson for acquiring Simmons.

The Bears, who have won five straight games, reshaped the capabilities of their defense on Oct. 29 when they sent their 2027 and 2028 first-round picks along with a fourth-rounder to the Titans in exchange for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The 29-year-old became the first defensive tackle to be traded for multiple first-round picks in the common draft era (since 1967).

After five straight losing seasons in Tennessee, Simmons was traded to a Bears team that went all-in ahead of the trade deadline to upgrade its roster for a run at Super Bowl LXI. His impact was felt immediately with five sacks over Chicago's three straight wins against Seattle, Tampa Bay and New Orleans, giving him a share of the team lead with Booker.

"This team believes in what they have here, and they want it right now," Simmons said. "My game, my passion, my energy, my leadership, I can only help this team even more than what it's got."

The Bears (8-2, 0-2) face a huge NFC North Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Detroit Lions (1 p.m. ET, CBS). Chicago is off to its best start in 20 years, although it's still looking for its first division win.

articles.headline: Joshua Kimmich blasts Bayern Munich over Jamal Musiala treatment: 'Absolute no-go'
articles.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's "not Bayern-like" treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.

Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO.

Now a key player has spoken out, too, and warned Bayern risks undermining its family image.

"What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public," Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday.

"It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either."

Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's run of injuries over the last two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, had more impact on his game than the neurological condition.

"It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself," Kimmich added.

Bayern met with Musiala's agents Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension.

Bayern said the club and Musiala's representatives both accept he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension.

"This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared," Bayern said.

Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the field in two preseason games, leaving players and fans alarmed.

- Bayern Munich, Jamal Musiala mess shows German champs at their worst

- Bayern Munich: Jamal Musiala's health 'top priority' amid contract doubts

- Injury-hit Bayern beaten by Lille to suffer first UCL loss

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue.

Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern's loss at Lille, which continued a bad week for Bayern.

Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern have lost the lead in the Bundesliga to Borussia Dortmund and have now slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings.

articles.headline: Joshua Zirkzee backs Senne Lammens: 'We didn't draw because of him'
articles.description: Joshua Zirkzee has said the Manchester United dressing room will rally around Senne Lammens after the goalkeeper's error against Sporting CP denied Mauricio Pochettino a first win as head coach.
articles.body:
Joshua Zirkzee has said the Manchester United dressing room will rally around Senne Lammens after the goalkeeper's error against Sporting CP denied Mauricio Pochettino a first win as head coach.

United were on course for a first victory away from home in the Champions League since 2021 before Lammens dropped a cross at the feet of striker Luis Suárez 10 minutes from time.

Lammens also gave away a penalty in the first half as United drew 2-2 on a chaotic night in Lisbon.

"In this moment, we just give him space," said Zirkzee.

"I'm not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne's a great kid. He's got a good head on him.  And we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. And we didn't draw because of him.

"This team is a family, so there's no one who will suffer by themselves. Mistakes happen. Let's go on to the next one. Senne's a great goalkeeper."

- Champions League talking points: Was this a good result for Man United?

- Mauricio Pochettino: Man United were 'punished' by officials in Sporting draw

While United were left to rue individual mistakes against Sporting, Pochettino was also critical of the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak.

The Polish official awarded Sporting two penalties and chalked off two United goals. The first, scored by Amad Diallo, was only ruled out because Marciniak wrongly blew for a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up.

Tielemans was booked during the incident before picking up a second yellow card in stoppage time. It was more frustration for United after Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes of the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool on Sunday.

Asked if there was a feeling that key decisions were going against United, Zirkzee said: "Yeah, we're in a place where it can feel like that pretty quick.

"But as I said, we've got a locker room that's built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. And if it's us against the world, so be it."

articles.headline: Soccer's main character this week: Jude Bellingham is in a new stratosphere
articles.description: Why are goals trending up in Europe? Is it because Jude Bellingham can seemingly score them from anywhere? Bill Connelly takes a look at the week that was.
articles.body:
Real Madrid are the only perfect team remaining. AS Roma have looked like one of the best teams in the competition but are 25th. Arsenal are below Real Betis, and Bayern Munich are below Club Brugge. Paris Saint-Germain, Barcelona and Liverpool are all in the top five ... and so are debutants Como.

The UEFA Champions League is a mix of sense and nonsense at the moment, but then again that can apply to other competitions as well. Brighton & Hove Albion and AFC Bournemouth are in the Premier League's top five, while Manchester United are in the relegation zone. Newly promoted Racing Santander are seventh in LaLiga, while Villarreal are 14th. Lazio are leading Serie A in a season in which their fans are protesting incompetent ownership.

It's not any fun when this sport makes too much sense, but let's try to make at least a little sense of what we saw from this week's Champions League action and what it means for all competitions in the weeks ahead. Here are the four(ish) main characters from the week that was.

- Talking Points: Was this a good result for Man United?

- Dawson: New coach, same chaos at Man United

- Marcotti: Bayern have handled Musiala situation poorly

Main character No. 1: Goals

Goals are great, and the Champions League has lots of them. Powerful goals and lucky goals, great counterattacks and scruffy, late set piece goals, disastrous goals and cathartic goals -- they're all my co-favorites.

Champions League Matchday 5 wasn't particularly prolific by this competition's standards: There were only 47 of them in 18 matches (1.31 per team), and 22 of 36 teams had the audacity to score either zero or one goal. This unacceptable funk drove the overall scoring average competition all the way down to ... a still-massive 1.88 goals per team. This remains a competition committed to wonderfully wide-open play.

A few weeks ago, I noted that while scoring in the Champions League has been off the charts for a while, it almost seems to be bleeding into the domestic game.

"The season is still young," I wrote, "but scoring is up 7.8% in Ligue 1, 8.0% in the Bundesliga, 10.0% in LaLiga, and a whopping 20.1% in the Eredivisie and 23.9% in Serie A. Most of the increase has come from open play, too -- it's not like teams are just earning a lot more penalties or something."

A couple of domestic matchdays later, this all remains the case. While scoring is stagnant in the Premier League, six other major leagues have seen serious scoring increases early this season.

Over the five leagues in question -- Spain's LaLiga, the German Bundesliga, Italy's Serie A, France's Ligue 1 and the Netherlands' Eredivisie (which was already quite prolific) -- scoring has increased by 13.6% from 1.43 goals per match (per team) to 1.62, and the increase has come almost entirely from open play (from 0.83 to 0.97). The increase has been particularly pronounced in Serie A, where scoring has lurched upward by 31%, from 1.21 to 1.59 (from 0.82 to 1.21 in open play).

I

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Barcelona among clubs eyeing Man United's Ayden Heaven
articles.description: Barcelona are interested in a loan move for Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Barcelona are interested in a loan move for Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven, and they're making moves alongside Real Madrid in the hope of signing Manchester City star Erling Haaland next summer.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move away from Manchester United, and Barcelona are interested in the center back, according to The Sun. The 20-year-old has been left on the bench in both of Mauricio Pochettino's matches since the Argentine took over at Old Trafford. Fulham are also interested in Heaven, with Calvin Bassey having been linked with a January move going the other way, although that is deemed unlikely due to the 26-year-old's importance to the Cottagers.

- Barcelona and Real Madrid are manoeuvring behind the scenes over a move for Manchester City striker Erling Haaland in 2027, according to TEAMtalk. Both Spanish giants are in regular contact through intermediaries as they remain hopeful that they can engineer a move for the 26-year-old. Liverpool, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain have also shown an interest in Haaland, but they and senior figures at the Etihad are aware that the Norway international wants to test himself in LaLiga.

- Arsenal, Tottenham Hotspur, Man City, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Juventus all had scouts watching Antonio Nusa as the winger scored a brace in RB Leipzig's 3-1 win over Lens, according to TEAMtalk. Atletico Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are also interested in the 21-year-old. Leipzig are aware of the growing interest in Nusa and are working on a potential new contract for the Norway international, whose existing deal runs until 2029.

- Liverpool, Manchester United and Newcastle United are all interested in Juventus winger Francisco Conceição, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. Jorge Mendes offered the 23-year-old to the Magpies for next June in a deal that could also allow Juve to permanently sign Nick Woltemade. Conceicao isn't thinking about his future and has even hinted at the possibility of staying with Juventus and trying to win trophies with the club.

- Napoli is the first club to make a move for Monza striker Gustavo Varela, but Juventus, AC Milan and Inter are also in the mix for the 21-year-old, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. There are also various Premier League clubs following Varela, while Como could look to him due to uncertainty around Moise Kean's injury situation. For Milan, Varela is seen as an alternative to Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi, while Inter would only move in the summer.

articles.headline: Packers' Parsons calls for accountability after Rams run wild
articles.description: "That wasn't a championship attitude, competitiveness, drive," Micah Parsons said of Green Bay allowing the Rams to rush for a season-high 241 yards.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Twelve snaps. That's all it took for Green Bay Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons to record his first sack since he ripped apart his left knee nearly a year ago.

Forty-seven runs. That's what it took for the Los Angeles Rams to keep Parsons from doing much more damage.

It ruined what had the makings of a storybook return by Parsons, and it put the Packers in a hole -- a "massive" one, as Parsons called it -- with just six games left in a season that might be slipping away.

On the way to a 26-13 victory over the Packers, the Rams rushed for a season-high 241 yards, led by Blake Corum, who ran for a career-high 184 and a touchdown on 32 carries.

"We need to figure out who's going to be a dog or not," Parsons said. "Like that's just the reality of it. To me, to be honest and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don't have an answer for it, that is player ... that's accountability. That's just how I really feel about it."

Parsons played just 26 of 71 defensive snaps (37%) in his first game since Week 15 of last season. He recorded four pressures, two quarterback hits and a sack of Matthew Stafford after he smoked left tackle Alaric Jackson with a speed move in the second quarter. Parsons was double-teamed on 56% of his pass rushes, according to ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats.

He would have liked to have played more.

The Packers' inability to stop the run prevented it.

"I wasn't able to get on the field because of it, because they didn't want to waste my plays on first and second down," Parsons said. "I think the whole thing is just bad and we've got to figure out who's willing to play with us or who's playing against us at this point because every quarter, every minute, every down matters and we've got to figure out who's in this for the long haul and who's in it for the ride."

The ride, however, could be a short one. The Packers' playoff chances plummeted with the loss. At 6-5, they have just a 19% chance to make the postseason, according to ESPN Analytics. The Packers would lose the head-to-head tiebreak with the Rams, whose playoff chances jumped to 55%, and the Minnesota Vikings (who swept the Packers).

"This hole is massive," Parsons said. "We took a big swing and we missed ginormously. The only way to get out is, we probably have to win out. That's just the reality of this situation. I think the people know that. We know that. From player to coach, we have to play better. It's not just the players. It's coaches, the whole thing, we have to all be better. I definitely look at that."

Jordan Love (two interceptions) and the running game (14 rushes for 55 yards) both struggled, and the Packers ran just 44 total offensive plays (including only 16 in the second half, when they managed just two first downs). articles.headline: Viktor Gyökeres: Arsenal not wasting energy on Man City's possible sanctions
articles.description: Viktor Gyökeres said Arsenal cannot afford to waste any energy on Manchester City's possible sanctions -- as he vowed to deliver back-to-back Premier League titles for the Gunners.
articles.body:
Viktor Gyökeres said Arsenal cannot afford to waste any energy on Manchester City's possible sanctions -- as he vowed to deliver back-to-back Premier League titles for the Gunners.

Arsenal will lock horns with City at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday for the first time since their rivals were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations in September.

City, who finished runners-up to Arsenal last season and are six points behind them heading into this weekend's mouth-watering contest, have appealed the verdict to leave the race for the title in limbo.

But when asked if City's potential punishment changes the outcome of the championship race, Gyökeres said: "No. It is what it is.

"We are focused on the game on Sunday. We can't control that. It has nothing to do with us. So, we don't put any energy into that."

City's campaign has unravelled since the club's guilty verdict, with Enzo Maresca's side taking just one win across their last seven games in all competitions, including a single point from a possible 12 in the Premier League.

But Gyökeres continued: "They still have a very good squad and very good players.

"Sometimes, you may have a period where you don't get the results all the time -- which is normal for any club.

"It is going to be a difficult game on Sunday. But it is always fun with big games. It is going to be good."

- Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

- Arteta questions 'how in hell' Arsenal didn't score more in Dortmund draw

- Erling Haaland: When Man City don't win 'you start questioning everything'

City's demise, and Arsenal's early advantage at the summit of the league, makes Mikel Arteta's side the clear favourite to successfully defend their Premier League crown for the first time in the club's history.

And when asked how hungry he and his teammates are to win back-to-back titles, the Sweden international -- who will hope to start Sunday's contest after he scored in Arsenal's 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday -- replied: "Of course, we always want to win titles and we know how tough it is in the Premier League with the games and the teams.

"But we have an amazing squad, amazing players, so that's the aim. We push each other every day to achieve that and we are definitely going to go for it.

"We always go into games wanting to win, and overall we have done well this season. Last season, we were on top of the league for most of the time. We are used to that position now and the main goal is to keep it that way and to win on Sunday."

articles.headline: Champions League talking points: Was this a good result for Man United?
articles.description: Gab Marcotti, Mark Ogden, Sam Tighe and Alex Kirkland run the rule over Man United's draw with Sporting, plus all the other moments that mattered from Matchday 5.
articles.body:
Matchday 5 of the UEFA Champions League league phase is in the books, with Real Madrid -- thanks in large part to some world-class play from Jude Bellingham -- topping the 36-team table with three games to play.

Barcelona and Lille notched some impressive wins, while it was a particularly forgettable round for the five Premier League teams in action; only Liverpool were able to secure all three points on offer, romping to an easy 3-0 victory over Club Brugge.

The telenovela that is Manchester United took another turn, and Arsenal and Manchester City prepared for what could be a pivotal clash Sunday with some stale performances.

So, what to make of it all? ESPN FC writers Gab Marcotti, Alex Kirkland, Mark Ogden and Sam Tighe are here to break down the action.

- As it happened: Another night of mayhem for Pochettino's Man United

- Lindop: Liverpool are all smiles as Wirtz, Isak start to click

- Olley: Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

Q1. Man United continue to entertain their haters and infuriate their fans even with the new hope of Mauricio Pochettino installed as manager. Except they were thumped at Anfield on Sunday (Leny Yoro's red card didn't help) and then had to battle back to get a 2-2 draw at Sporting CP with a Youri Tielemans red card, a string of individual errors, a disallowed goal, and a dodgy referee making for another wild 90 minutes. Is it going to get worse before it gets better for Poch & Co.?

Marcotti: I think we can let Man United take a mulligan for Pochettino's first two games. He has been there less than a week, going two goals and a man down at Anfield so quickly made the game meaningless and, against Sporting, they were without Matheus Cunha and Marcus Rashford and the game was straight out of the bizarro world.

Referee Szymon Marciniak has a big reputation, but he obviously had a rough night -- though nowhere near as bad the commentators on my TV made it seem. I thought Amad Diallo's goal should have stood, but I thought Kaique was fouled for the other disallowed goal. Tielemans shouldn't be tackling that way when on a yellow, that should be obvious. And, of course, Bruno Fernandes' goal was a total fluke.

Tighe: If I were Pochettino, I'd be as perplexed as I am fuming over how the first week on the job has gone. Liverpool away was over before it began due to a refereeing mistake, then a bunch more refereeing mistakes also threatened to pull the rug on Wednesday's game.

Tielemans' red card was their fifth of the season so far, and it's only November. We panned Chelsea last season for their ludicrous lack of discipline and we should do the same for United (even if Yoro's was incorrectly given, the count is still four).

This is a team that too easily implodes or shoots itself in the foot. Every game they play, they do something that makes the next one harder. It's really hard to win top-level football games when you do that, and who's next up? Brentford ... Pochettino's pain might endure

articles.headline: Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino
articles.description: Manchester United showed signs of progress under Mauricio Pochettino, but familiar mistakes cost them a Champions League win against Sporting CP.
articles.body:
LISBON, Portugal -- Mauricio Pochettino must wonder what he has walked into.

Just a week and two games into his role as Manchester United head coach, he will have learned already that chaos is never far away.

His plan for Liverpool on Sunday went out the window when Leny Yoro was controversially sent off after just eight minutes. Pochettino's second game, against Sporting CP in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, included three penalties, two costly goalkeeping errors, two disallowed goals and another red card.

Pochettino will have been encouraged by some of the things he saw in the 2-2 draw at Estadio José Alvalade. But there will also be a deepened sense that his players can often make things hard for themselves at the worst possible moment.

He has admitted to sleepless nights since making the whirlwind transition from being the United States national team head coach. You can understand why.

"It's a good welcome for us after seven days, no?" Pochettino said after Wednesday's topsy-turvy draw.

"I'm so excited to be in front and be the face of representing this club. I think we are here because the situation wasn't the situation that all the fans and the people expected.

"That is why we are here and we are here to take the responsibility from one week," the coach added, "and we are going to, for sure, improve and to put again the team in the place that because of the history and everything they deserve to be. It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy."

He's not wrong. Pochettino insisted at his prematch conference Tuesday that his players aren't "fragile," but there was evidence again that confidence is in short supply. It's something he needs to fix quickly.

Encouraging signs, costly mistakes

The opening 30 minutes were reassuringly calm. But this is a United team that at times has seemed determined to find trouble wherever they can. They did so again.

In the first half, Sporting were awarded two penalties in the space of 75 seconds. One was harsh, the other given after a reckless decision from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Both were avoidable.

The two situations came from Sporting players taking advantage of having time on the ball to play sweeping forward passes. United were punished only once, with Luis Suárez missing the first spot kick and scoring the second.

The self-sabotage wasn't over.

United went ahead thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a bizarre second when the midfielder's long-range shot hit a divot and bounced over Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira.

But just as they got within sight of a first Champions League away win since 2021, Lammens dropped a harmless cross at Suárez's feet.

If Pochettino is going to turn things around, he needs his players to cut out the individual mistakes. There were plenty at Anfield on Sunday, even if the Argentine coach was keener to focus on the performance of the referee.

He wasn't helped by the officiating here. Amad Diallo had a goal ruled out by Polish referee Szymon

articles.headline: Luis Enrique praises Roma after draw halts PSG's winning streak
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique said Roma was his team's "toughest match of this season" after a hard-fought 2-2 Champions League draw on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique praised AS Roma for handing the defending Champions League title holder their toughest test of the season after the Italian side snapped PSG's 12-game winning streak with a 2-2 draw on Wednesday.

"Without any doubt this was our toughest match of this season, in the Champions League or the French league. I am happy with the result, and the merit goes to Roma," Luis Enrique said.

"Facing a team with this attitude and this kind of mentality is very hard to play against. It's very different to the kind of match we're used to."

Roma striker Donyell Malen secured the point in the 78th minute, blasting in a penalty to end a dominant run in which PSG had not dropped points since losing at home to Monaco on Sept. 4.

Luis Enrique also lauded Roma counterpart Gian Piero Gasperini's tactical setup and said he hopes to face him again in the knockout rounds.

"It's the first time I've come up against him as a coach," he said before pausing and nodding in respect.

"It's better to talk about Roma's future, not PSG's. Roma's future is wonderful; they can win the Scudetto. I have no doubt they can finish in the top 24, I hope so, and I wouldn't like to face them again. Maybe in the final," the Spanish coach added.

Malen, who entered midway through the second half after scoring four goals in a 5-1 win at Parma on Saturday, found the net again with his 17th goal in 16 games this season, including five in the Champions League.

"At the moment he is among the very best strikers in the world, with his ability to score goals, his pace, the speed with which he shoots as well," Gasperini said. "He took a bit of time to get going when he came on, but by the end we saw the real Malen. He took the penalty very well."

Gasperini explained that he held Malen back until the second half because of his heavy workload for Roma and the Netherlands.

"I go back to Rome very, very happy tonight," Gasperini said. "It was a great performance against a team which is no doubt the best in the world at the moment. It was an important test and a very difficult one for us."

Before kickoff, PSG's ultras boldly displayed a giant tifo depicting two bloodied Roman gladiators -- the victorious figure dressed in PSG's blue, white, and red, and the defeated gladiator kneeling with bowed head in Roma's red and gold.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.
